pl-l2d22c3-d1e108.summary: Asks whether such pride and love of his own power was in the man as in the woman.

pl-l2d22c3-d1e111.summary: Answers that Adam was not seduced as the woman was, since he did not think the devil's suggestion true; yet he may be said deceived in thinking venial what was deadly. He was neither first seduced nor in her way, but was a transgressor; some pride could have arisen in him right after the temptation, making him want to try the forbidden tree when he saw the woman did not die.
claims: Adam did not believe the devil.
Adam may have thought the sin venial.

pl-l2d22c3-d1e120.summary: Cites Augustine: Paul calls Adam a transgressor but denies he was seduced; asked, he said not 'the woman seduced me' but 'she gave me and I ate,' while the woman said 'the serpent seduced me.'
claims: Adam was not seduced; the woman was.

pl-l2d22c3-d1e148.summary: Further Augustine: seduction properly means taking a false suggestion as true, that God forbade the tree because they would become gods, as if envying them divinity. Even if the man, because of some pride, was moved by a desire to experience when he saw the woman did not die, he did not, if spiritually minded, believe what the devil suggested.
claims: Seduction is believing a falsehood true.
Adam did not believe the devil's suggestion.

pl-l2d22c3.summary: Asks whether such pride was in the man as in the woman. Adam was not seduced as she was: he did not think the devil's suggestion true, though he may have been deceived in thinking the sin venial when it was mortal. Yet he was a transgressor (Rom 5:14), and some pride may have arisen in him after the temptation, making him want to try the tree when he saw the woman did not die. Augustine: Paul calls Adam a transgressor but not seduced (1 Tim 2:14); 'seduction' is believing the false suggestion true; Adam may have been moved by desire to experience, but did not believe the devil.
claims: Adam was not seduced as the woman was.
Adam did not believe the devil's suggestion.
Adam may have been deceived in thinking the sin venial.
Some pride or desire to experience may have moved him after the temptation.
